children: The S&P 500 pushed to a fresh record Tuesday as technology shares extended their rally, keeping Wall Street's AI-driven momentum intact ahead of fresh comments from Federal Reserve officials. Falling Treasury yields provided another tailwind for equities, though weakness in energy and sharp moves in individual stocks showed investors are becoming increasingly selective beneath the headline indexes.
The S&P 500 rose about 0.8%, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8% and also touched a record high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced roughly 0.5%.
Market breadth was relatively strong, with nine of the S&P 500's 11 sectors trading higher. Utilities led gains, while energy was the weakest group as crude oil prices declined.

Technology remains central to the market's advance as investors continue betting that heavy spending on artificial intelligence will translate into stronger corporate earnings. Expectations for a solid upcoming earnings season have helped maintain risk appetite even with major indexes already trading near record levels.

Bond markets also offered stocks some relief Tuesday. The 2-year Treasury yield declined 2 basis points to 4.78%, while the benchmark 10-year yield fell 4 basis points to 5.26%. The 30-year yield slipped 2 basis points to 5.64%.
Lower yields can provide particular support for technology and other growth stocks by reducing the discount rate applied to their future earnings.
Individual moves were much larger. Constellation Energy (CEG) surged more than 13%, while Seagate Technology (STX) dropped roughly 7%.
The next test for the rally is whether record index levels can survive a combination of elevated Treasury yields, upcoming earnings and shifting expectations for Federal Reserve policy.

Investors should watch whether market participation continues broadening beyond mega-cap technology. Nine sectors advancing Tuesday is encouraging, but sustained records become more durable when earnings growth spreads across industries.

Fed commentary is the immediate catalyst. A more dovish rate outlook could push yields lower and support expensive growth stocks, while renewed inflation concerns or a higher-for-longer stance could challenge valuations.

Corporate earnings remain the bigger fundamental test. Strong guidance could validate the rally; disappointments from heavily weighted technology companies could quickly expose how much optimism is already embedded in prices.

title: S&P 500 Breaks Record Ahead of Crucial Fed Test
